note: Settings > AI brain: a Link and a Prompt button per provider. 'link' opens in the browser. 'prompt' (an array of lines, joined with newlines) is copied to the clipboard for the player to give to a coding agent, and 'prompt_intro' is shown when it is. Each prompt asks only for a running server and the URL and model name to paste into F10.
prompt_intro: Give this to a coding agent with access to the internet and your computer, in a trusted location (e.g. ~/projects/desert-spaceport).

ollama.title: Ollama
prompt: Set up Ollama on this computer with a model my game can use as its AI. When it works, give me two values to paste into the game's settings: the Ollama URL and the Ollama model name. That is the whole job: do not edit the game's files and do not install anything the steps below do not need.
WHAT THE GAME NEEDS FROM OLLAMA
- Ollama's OpenAI-compatible API. The game sends POST <Ollama URL>/chat/completions, adding "/chat/completions" itself, so the URL you give me ends in /v1.
- Streaming and structured output ("response_format": {"type": "json_schema", ...}). Use a current Ollama release.
- Speed. The game gives up on a reply if the first token takes more than 4 seconds. That includes loading the model if Ollama has unloaded it, which it does after 5 idle minutes by default.
- Localhost only. Leave Ollama listening on 127.0.0.1 (its default).
STEPS
1. Check the machine: OS, chip and GPU (Apple Silicon; NVIDIA and its VRAM; AMD; or CPU only), RAM, and free disk. Tell me what you found before you download anything big.

2. Install Ollama from https://ollama.com/download (on macOS, brew install ollama also works). Make sure the server is running: curl http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/tags returns JSON. The desktop app runs it on macOS and Windows. On Linux the installer sets up a systemd service.

3. Choose a model. Use an instruct (non-thinking) model. Thinking models spend seconds reasoning before the first word and will miss the limit. Check the exact current tags on https://ollama.com/library before you pull.
- Under 32 GB of RAM (or a GPU under 16 GB): a 4B instruct model, for example a Qwen3 4B "instruct-2507" tag or gemma3:4b. About 3 GB.
- 32 GB or more (Apple Silicon, or a GPU with 24 GB or more): a Qwen3 30B-A3B "instruct-2507" tag, about 19 GB, fast because only 3B parameters are active per token, or gemma3:12b.

- Avoid plain hybrid tags that think by default (such as qwen3:4b) unless you have checked thinking is off. Tell me which model you picked and why, check there is enough free disk, then ollama pull <tag>.
4. Test it the way the game will:
- ollama list shows the tag.
- Send a streamed request with a JSON schema, and time it:

curl -N http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1/chat/completions -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"<tag>","stream":true,"max_tokens":60,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Greet a traveller in one short sentence."}],"response_format":{"type":"json_schema","json_schema":{"name":"reply","strict":true,"schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"say":{"type":"string"}},"required":["say"]}}}}'

- It should stream valid JSON such as {"say": "..."}. Time the first token twice: once after the model was unloaded (ollama stop <tag> first), and once with it loaded. The loaded time must be well under 4 seconds. If the cold time is over 4 seconds, tell me. Then ask before setting OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE (for example 30m, or -1 for always) so the model stays loaded; it keeps that much memory in use.
5. Make sure Ollama starts with the computer (the app or service usually does), and tell me how to check it is running.
WHAT TO GIVE ME AT THE END
Exactly these two lines, with the real values:
Ollama URL: http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1
Ollama model: gemma3:4b
What is allowed:

- Ollama URL: http:// plus the host and port, ending in /v1, with no /chat/completions and no trailing slash. Use 127.0.0.1 or localhost, and port 11434 unless OLLAMA_HOST changed it. Use another machine's address (for example http://192.168.1.20:11434/v1) only if I asked for that.
- Ollama model: the tag exactly as ollama list prints it, name:tag. A name with no tag means :latest. Examples: gemma3:4b, gemma3:12b, qwen3:30b-a3b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M.
Then tell me to open the game, press F10, paste the two values into Ollama URL and Ollama model, turn on "AI characters", set Mode to ollama, and press Save and then Test.

local.title: Local server (llama.cpp)
prompt: Set up a llama.cpp server (llama-server) on this computer so my game can use it as its local AI model. When it works, give me two values to paste into the game's settings: the Local URL and the Local model name. That is the whole job: do not edit the game's files and do not install anything the steps below do not need.
WHAT THE GAME NEEDS FROM THE SERVER
- OpenAI-compatible API. The game sends POST <Local URL>/chat/completions, adding "/chat/completions" itself, so the URL you give me ends in /v1.
- Streaming ("stream": true) and structured output ("response_format": {"type": "json_schema", ...}), which llama-server turns into a grammar. Use a current llama.cpp build.
- Speed. The game gives up on a reply if the first token takes more than 2.5 seconds, so the model must be fast on this machine, not just fit in memory.
- Localhost only. The server listens on 127.0.0.1; do not expose it to the network.
STEPS
1. Check the machine: OS, chip and GPU (Apple Silicon; NVIDIA and its VRAM; AMD; or CPU only), RAM, and free disk. Tell me what you found before you download anything big.
2. Install llama.cpp.
- macOS: brew install llama.cpp

- Windows or Linux: the latest release from https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases that matches the GPU (CUDA for NVIDIA, Vulkan for AMD or Intel, CPU otherwise). Put it in a stable folder and tell me the full path to llama-server.
- Check: llama-server --version
3. Choose a model. Use an instruct (non-thinking) model in GGUF format at Q4_K_M. Thinking models spend seconds reasoning before the first word and will miss the 2.5 second limit.
- Under 32 GB of RAM (or a GPU under 16 GB): Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507, about 2.5 GB. https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507-GGUF (file Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507-Q4_K_M.gguf)

- 32 GB or more (Apple Silicon, or a GPU with 24 GB or more): Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507, about 18 GB. It is fast because only 3B parameters are active per token. https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-GGUF (file Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-Q4_K_M.gguf)
- A newer non-thinking instruct model of the same size is fine too. Tell me which one you picked and why, check there is enough free disk, then download it into a stable folder such as ~/models/.
4. Start the server:
llama-server --model <path to .gguf> --alias <model name> --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8088 --ctx-size 8192 --n-gpu-layers 99 --jinja
- Port 8088 is the game's default, so the URL then needs no change. If 8088 is taken by something else, use another free port.
- --alias is the model name you will give me. Keep it short with no spaces, for example cantina-owner or qwen3-4b.
- On a machine with no usable GPU, use --n-gpu-layers 0.
5. Test it the way the game will:
- curl http://127.0.0.1:8088/health should return {"status":"ok"} once the model has loaded.
- curl http://127.0.0.1:8088/v1/models should list the alias.
- Send a streamed request with a JSON schema, and time it:

curl -N http://127.0.0.1:8088/v1/chat/completions -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"<model name>","stream":true,"max_tokens":60,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Greet a traveller in one short sentence."}],"response_format":{"type":"json_schema","json_schema":{"name":"reply","strict":true,"schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"say":{"type":"string"}},"required":["say"]}}}}'

- It should stream valid JSON such as {"say": "..."}. Run it twice. The time to the first token on the second run must be under 2.5 seconds. If it is not, fix GPU offload or pick a smaller model, and tell me what you changed.

6. Keep it running. The game uses the server whenever I play, and it does not start this one for me. Give me the exact command to start it again. Then ask whether I want it to start by itself at login (a launchd agent on macOS, a Task Scheduler task on Windows, a systemd user service on Linux), and set that up only if I say yes.
WHAT TO GIVE ME AT THE END
Exactly these two lines, with the real values:
Local model: cantina-owner
What is allowed:

- Local URL: http:// plus the host and port, ending in /v1, with no /chat/completions and no trailing slash. Use 127.0.0.1 or localhost. Use another machine's address only if I asked for that. Examples: http://127.0.0.1:8088/v1, http://localhost:8080/v1.
- Local model: the --alias you set, exactly as /v1/models lists it. Examples: cantina-owner, qwen3-4b, qwen3-30b-a3b.
Then tell me to open the game, press F10, paste the two values into Local URL and Local model, turn on "AI characters", set Mode to local, and press Save and then Test.

cloud.title: Cloud (Claude API)
prompt: Help me connect my game to a cloud AI model through the Claude API. I create the account and the API key myself. Your job is to guide me and then give me the values to paste into the game's settings. That is the whole job: do not edit the game's files and do not install anything.
WHAT THE GAME NEEDS
- Four settings: Cloud URL, Cloud model, Cloud type and Cloud key. With the Claude API the type is anthropic, and the game sends POST <Cloud URL>/messages, adding "/messages" itself.

- Speed and cost. The game streams replies and gives up if the first token takes more than 5 seconds, and every line of dialogue is a request of a few thousand tokens. Use the newest fast, low-cost model, which is the Haiku tier.
STEPS
1. Open https://platform.claude.com in my browser. I sign in or sign up, add billing (prepaid credits), and create an API key on the API Keys page. It starts with sk-ant-.
- Do not sign in, create the account, enter payment details or create the key for me.
- Never ask me to paste the key into this chat, a file or a command you run. It goes straight into the game.
2. Suggest that I set a monthly spend limit in the console, and tell me roughly what a play session costs at the model's current per-token price.
3. Look up the current model list in the Claude docs (the Models page, linked from platform.claude.com) and pick the newest Haiku model. Use its exact API model id, not its display name.
WHAT TO GIVE ME AT THE END
Exactly these lines, with the real model id:
Cloud URL: https://api.anthropic.com/v1
Cloud model: claude-haiku-5-5
Cloud type: anthropic
Cloud key: the key you created (starts with sk-ant-), pasted only into the game
What is allowed:

- Cloud URL: https://api.anthropic.com/v1 for the Claude API, with no /messages and no trailing slash. An OpenAI-compatible service also works: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 with type openai_compat, its own key (sk-or-...) and its model ids (for example anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5). Use that only if I ask.
- Cloud model: an exact API model id. Examples: claude-haiku-5-5, claude-sonnet-5-5.

Then tell me to open the game, press F10, and paste the key into Cloud key. Pasting an sk-ant- key fills in the URL, type and model by itself, so I only check them against your values. Then turn on "AI characters", tick "Cloud enabled", set Mode to cloud, and press Save and then Test. The game keeps the key in its own settings folder, never in the project.
